title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles were deployed into a high-traffic event without contingency planning for extreme congestion. When Fourth of July celebrations created unexpected road closures and gridlock near the Golden Gate Bridge, multiple vehicles' batteries depleted while stuck in standstill traffic, requiring towing assistance. The company had not anticipated or prepared for the traffic volume generated by the event.

This deployment failure occurred in the operational decision layer, not the vehicle control system. Waymo relied on routing and battery management assumptions built from normal traffic patterns, then sent vehicles into conditions that violated those assumptions. It would have required either real-time event awareness integrated into routing, battery reserve policies for uncertain conditions, or a choice not to operate during major celebrations when traffic patterns are knowably unpredictable.

It is not established whether this incident results from a gap in Waymo's planning, inadequate coordination with the city, insufficient driver training, or some combination. The reports also describe a vehicle catching fire after driving over fireworks and a passenger discomfort with nearby fireworks, but do not clarify whether these represent separate control failures or consequences of the stranding itself.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
During Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco on Saturday, multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded in heavy traffic following fireworks displays near the Golden Gate Bridge. Video footage showed at least a dozen vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets with depleted batteries, requiring towing assistance. The company attributed the situation to major traffic disruptions, high volume of travelers, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion. Waymo stated it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during major traffic events.

The incident highlighted challenges autonomous vehicles face in crisis situations. Residents reported frustration with stationary Waymo cars blocking roads, with some motorists waiting nearly two hours in standstill traffic. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks on the road. Additionally, a passenger experienced a safety concern when her Waymo continued driving as fireworks exploded nearby. San Francisco's mayor acknowledged the traffic problems and said city officials will discuss the incident with public and private partners to prevent similar disruptions in the future.
